title: prefill/decode pipeline: chunked speculative prefill + stage-overlap + kernel scheduler + KV-cache tuning
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Performance: Improved end-to-end throughput and p99 latency for mixed prefill+decode workloads via chunked speculative prefill, stage overlap, kernel scheduling heuristics, and KV-cache eviction/lookup optimizations.
description: Context: Prefill and decode stages in the serving runtime are a major source of tail latency for streaming and long-context workloads. Previous work introduced speculative prefill and stage overlap independently; this PR combines chunked prefill, speculative prefill, stage overlap, and a lightweight kernel scheduler and KV-cache tuning to reduce stall time and improve utilization. Motivation: Customers running mixed workloads (long prefill followed by interactive decode) observed high p99 latency spikes and poor GPU kernel utilization. This change aims to reduce end-to-end latency while keeping token cost neutral and preserving generation quality. What changed (summary): - Introduce chunked prefill: break long prefill input into smaller prefill chunks to enable earlier start of decode paths and better KV-cache locality. - Speculative prefill continuation: allow decode to speculatively start on earlier chunks when the rest of the prefill is not expected to change model state, reducing time-to-first-token. - Stage overlap improvements: better coordination between prefill and decode workers so GPU kernels for decode can be enqueued while prefill kernels finish remaining chunks. - Kernel scheduler heuristics: lightweight cost model that prefers short-latency decode kernels when overlap potential is high, and defers large prefill kernels when it would block progress. - KV-cache tuning: reduce lock contention on KV cache lookups, add per-worker small LRU for hot spans, and tweak eviction window for chunked prefill patterns. - Metrics and benchmarks: added microbenchmarks and end-to-end bench harnesses to measure throughput and tail latency for mixed workloads. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for new scheduler heuristics and KV-cache behavior added under runtime/tests. - New perf harness runs comparing baseline vs this branch across multiple sequence lengths and batch mixes. Results: - Mixed workload (1x long prefill 8k tokens + 8x interactive decodes): observed ~22% improvement in steady throughput and ~35% reduction in p99 latency for decode-first response times on T4/GPU cluster in our perf lab. - Kernel utilization improved from 64% -> 78% on average for the examined trace. Backwards compatibility and safety: - All new behaviors are guarded behind the runtime config flags: enable_chunked_prefill, enable_speculative_prefill, and kernel_scheduler_mode (off|conservative|aggressive). Defaults remain conservative (off for speculative) to avoid regressions. - Added a rollback path to revert to legacy prefill/decode pipeline if a rollout experiment shows regressions. Migration: - No API changes. Customers controlling behavior can opt in via runtime config. Checklist: - [x] Design doc referenced ENG-7342 and perf notes - [x] Unit tests - [x] Perf benchmarks - [x] Docs/console knobs added - [x] CI green on final run Notes: This PR composes multiple optimizations; individual commits are small and focused so reviewers can follow per-area changes. See commit list and file summaries below.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Can you explain the safety checks for speculative prefill when inputs mutate during prefill? We need a deterministic fallback if the model state diverges.

Maya Chen: Reply: speculative start requires the prefill chunk to be marked immutable (no streaming edits from client) and we validate tokenization hash; if mismatch we abort speculative decode and fall back to waiting for full prefill. Added unit test to verify abort path.
Alyssa Park: The kernel scheduler looks promising, but please add telemetry to count scheduler decisions and time spent in scheduling path. Also ensure the conservative mode is effectively a no-op.
Maya Chen: Added runtime.kernel_schedule_decisions and runtime.kernel_schedule_latency metrics. Conservative mode skips scheduling and preserves previous dispatch behavior.
Jonah Reed: Observed small regression in a corner case with very short prefill (<16 tokens) where chunking adds overhead. Suggest bypass chunking for sequences <64 tokens.
Maya Chen: Adjusted chunking threshold to 64 tokens and added perf test that benchmarks short vs chunked to avoid regressions.
ci_checks: perf-regression: pass (this branch shows improvements vs baseline on perf infra)
bench_results_summary: Mixed-workload perf lab: throughput +22%, decode p99 -35% on T4; kernel utilization +14 percentage points. Microbench: chunked prefill overhead <1% on long sequences, negative for short sequences unless threshold bypassed.
notes_for_cherry_pick: This change touches low-level runtime kernels; backports to release/* require coordination. Recommended to cherry-pick only kernel_scheduler and KV-cache locking fixes separately; chunked/speculative features should land behind flags on stable branches.
manual_rollback_steps: 1) Disable enable_speculative_prefill and enable_chunked_prefill=false via runtime config; 2) If issues persist, revert the kernel_scheduler toggle to 'off' and restart runtime; 3) If needed, roll back the release to previous image.
merge_details: merged by Diego Morales via squash on 2025-11-18. Commit message summarized: combine chunked/speculative prefill, stage overlap, kernel scheduler, and KV-cache optimizations to improve mixed-workload tail latency and utilization.
notes: Follow-up work: (1) automatic rollout tuning to pick scheduler mode based on deployment-level SLOs, (2) deeper kernel fusion experiments to further reduce kernel launch overhead, (3) explore intra-GPU shared L2 caching heuristics for KV spans.
